item.title: TIB: Money and muscle power increasingly influence political parties
item.description:
The growing influence of money and muscle power in Bangladesh's political landscape is raising concerns over democratic practices within political parties, with a new study identifying gaps in internal democracy, financial transparency and accountability.
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) presented the findings in a report titled Institutional Governance of Political Parties in Bangladesh at a press conference in Dhanmondi, Dhaka, on Sunday.
The report found that political parties lack clear guidelines on financial management, income and expenditure records, auditing and accountability. It also identified a lack of effective mechanisms to prevent individuals involved in criminal activities from joining parties or securing important positions.
According to the study, 16 political parties do not regularly hold national conferences. Among them, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has not held a national conference in more than 10 years.
The parties also do not prepare annual budgets, with a large portion of their income and expenditure managed through program-based and informal processes.
The study found that the constitutions of 18 political parties do not specify minimum integrity and moral standards for membership. Nor do they contain effective provisions to prevent individuals involved in criminal activities from becoming members or holding important positions.
The report said political parties are increasingly seeking individuals with money and muscle power to finance party activities, meet expenses, establish dominance and control polling centers during elections.
At the same time, individuals who accumulate wealth through illegal means and possess muscle power seek political influence to secure protection and gain social standing.
Individuals involved in crimes such as extortion, human trafficking, smuggling, and arms and drug trading have also been found joining relatively influential political parties, the study said.
It further found that between 18% and 32% of candidates who contested the past 5 national parliamentary elections had at least 1 case filed against them over alleged involvement in various crimes.
TIB identified widespread shortcomings in the financial management of political parties, saying none of the parties studied had clear financial policies or procedures.
Their constitutions contain unclear provisions on income and expenditure, membership fees, donation acceptance, financial transactions, form fees, auditing and financial accountability.
The report also found that parties lack effective mechanisms to hold nominated candidates accountable for violating state regulations, including electoral codes of conduct.
Candidates have also concealed or provided incorrect and incomplete information in election affidavits about their assets, loans, business interests and foreign citizenship, it said.
Party constitutions also lack clear guidelines on candidates' election expenditure plans, sources of funds, expenditure monitoring and the submission of financial reports.
According to the study, candidates spent an average of 169.5% more than the prescribed expenditure limit in the 13th National Parliamentary Election, but political parties took no effective action over the violations.
TIB also found that parties rarely take visible action against allegations that their leaders and activists accumulate wealth through criminal activities, irregularities and corruption. In some cases, minor disciplinary measures are imposed to close the matter.
The study found shortcomings in political parties' disclosure of information. Of the 32 parties included in the research, 24 have websites, but only 16 are active.
Its overall findings point to extensive gaps in transparency, accountability, democratic practices, participation and inclusion in the institutional activities of political parties, alongside inadequate measures to prevent irregularities and corruption.
Although laws and regulations govern party registration and participation in national elections, the report identified the absence of a strong legal framework to ensure internal democracy, transparency and accountability in political financing.
It also said the existing legal framework does not fully align with international good practices.
Despite the substantial funds required to run political parties, much of their financial management depends on informal processes and individual arrangements. This creates significant discrepancies between officially disclosed income and expenditure and the actual financial situation, the report said.
The dominance of individual dependence and informal funding sources is also contributing to the development of individual- and family-centered politics within parties.
The study further identified the growing influence of black money, misuse of power, political criminalization and internal conflicts, particularly within influential political parties.
In many cases, political participation and party positions are increasingly becoming power-centered business models, it said.
Progress in women's political participation also remains limited, despite legal obligations and party commitments. The report said parties remain reluctant to ensure women's inclusion, with their presence in some party activities being largely nominal or symbolic.
Shortcomings in democratic practices, grassroots participation and the inclusion of female activists are further reinforcing single-person leadership, dynastic politics, authoritarianism, oligarchy and patriarchy within political parties, the study observed.
The study was conducted using qualitative methods, drawing on information from primary and secondary sources.
TIB contacted 42 political parties, including 37 registered and 5 unregistered parties, and received information from 32. The remaining 10 did not provide information despite repeated attempts to contact them.
The report also noted delays, non-cooperation and the submission of partial information by political parties and relevant stakeholders during data collection.
Information was collected in 2 phases: the first from June 2023 to February 2024 and the second from June 2025 to September 2026.
Speaking at the press conference, TIB Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman said political parties are among the most important institutions in a democratic system.
He said political parties had made significant contributions to Bangladesh's history and achievements, while also bearing responsibility for various challenges to democratic progress and good governance.
“Democracy cannot be properly implemented if good governance is not ensured within political parties, which are among the central institutions of the democratic system,” he said.
“We generally talk about reforms in various state institutions, but the issue of internal reforms within political parties is often overlooked. However, institutional good governance within political parties is extremely important for establishing democracy,” he added.
Iftekharuzzaman said the study considered the roles of political parties and people's expectations of them.
He said the research began in June 2023, but changes in the country's political context and challenges in obtaining cooperation from political parties during information collection prolonged the process of completing the report.

item.title: Titumir: Govt to implement reforms with five stakeholders to ensure sustainable LDC graduation
item.description:
The government has undertaken a comprehensive reform initiative involving five key stakeholders - the people, private sector, United Nations, development partners and multilateral development institutions - to ensure Bangladesh's sustainable graduation from the Least Developed Country (LDC) category.
The government does not want to treat the additional three years granted for LDC graduation preparation merely as an extension of time. Instead, it aims to utilise the period to implement structural reforms in the economy, enhance productivity, explore new markets and lay the foundation for long-term sustainable development.
Prime Minister's Adviser on Finance and Planning Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir said this in an interview at the Bangladesh Secretariat on Sunday.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had set a vision of transforming Bangladesh into a global manufacturing hub and an export gateway. To achieve this goal, the government is working on a strategy to transform the country from "graduation to a trillion-dollar economy", while ensuring that the transformation remains sustainable.
Titumir said Bangladesh has the largest economy among the LDCs and, therefore, requires major reforms to diversify its economy, enhance competitiveness and increase productivity.
Explaining the rationale for the extended preparation period, the adviser said the government considers it an integral part of its broader economic strategy.
He identified three key considerations behind the decision: domestic economic vulnerabilities inherited from the previous administration, external pressures and economic uncertainties arising from the Middle East crisis, and the country's inadequate preparation to address these challenges.
"Taking these realities into consideration, the government has started working on the necessary measures. However, the government has supported LDC graduation from the very beginning," he said.
Regarding reform priorities, the Prime Minister's adviser said restoring discipline in the banking sector and ensuring adequate financing for investment are among the government's major objectives.
The government will also focus on strengthening energy security, exploring new investment markets and diversifying the country's export basket. It will pursue free trade agreements (FTAs) with different countries to mitigate the possible loss of trade preferences following LDC graduation.
Titumir said achieving these objectives would become easier through an effective compact with the private sector.
He said private sector representatives had been involved in every discussion on LDC graduation, adding that the initiative also forms part of the government's "Three Rs" strategy.
The adviser said the government had brought five stakeholders under the reform initiative: the people of Bangladesh, the private sector, the United Nations, development partners and multilateral development institutions.
He described the initiative as an unprecedented consensus-based partnership.
Highlighting the role of the United Nations, Titumir said a unanimously adopted proposal had mandated the UN system to provide all forms of support, including technical assistance, to Bangladesh's graduation preparations. The UN Resident Coordinator will lead the coordination of this assistance.
He said the International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Bank, Asian Development Bank (ADB), Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) and Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) had assured support for the priority reforms identified by the government.
Titumir added that the ongoing IMF programme and other reform initiatives were aligned with the government's broader reform agenda.
He said the reforms were being undertaken on the basis of the people's mandate, which was one of the distinctive features of the initiative.
"Never before have the people of the country been involved in reform initiatives in this manner," he said, adding that the participation of the five stakeholders would also help strengthen confidence among foreign investors.
The adviser identified energy security as a major prerequisite for sustainable industrialisation and investment.
He said the government planned to develop energy infrastructure centred on Matarbari while expanding the necessary facilities in other parts of the country.
To increase LNG import capacity, the government is working on establishing land-based LNG terminals alongside floating storage and regasification facilities.
The government is also prioritising increased solar power generation, reducing wastage and system losses in the energy supply chain, and diversifying sources of LNG imports.
Titumir said developing energy infrastructure beyond Matarbari, particularly in the southwestern region and other parts of the country, would create opportunities for geographically balanced industrialisation.
He said the government was also focusing on exploring new export destinations and pursuing FTAs or Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements (CEPAs) with trading partners to address the potential reduction of duty-free and quota-free market access after LDC graduation.
The additional three years, he said, have created an important economic opportunity for Bangladesh.
Proper utilisation of the extended period could help strengthen the country's economic foundations through higher investment, new export markets, expanded production capacity and increased employment opportunities.
The period, therefore, represents not only an opportunity to prepare for LDC graduation but also a crucial window for Bangladesh's long-term economic transformation.

item.title: Editors' Council urges restraint after PM aide tears up Amar Desh copy
item.description:
The Editors' Council has called for restraint and mutual respect in expressing differences of opinion after Prime Minister's Political Assistant Rashed Khan was seen tearing up a copy of the daily newspaper Amar Desh in a video posted on his Facebook page on Saturday.
In a statement signed by Editors' Council President Nurul Kabir and General Secretary Dewan Hanif Mahmud, the council said disagreeing with news reports or editorial opinions was a democratic right.
However, it stressed the importance of maintaining responsibility, decency and mutual respect when expressing differences of opinion.
The council said that as the prime minister's political assistant and a person holding the rank of secretary, Rashed Khan was expected to demonstrate restraint and responsibility in his statements and conduct.
It also emphasized the importance of maintaining professional standards, objectivity, ethics and accountability in journalism.
The Editors' Council called on all concerned to refrain from provocative statements, threats and harassment, and to uphold media freedom and the safety of journalists.

item.title: Sajek gunfight continues for second day, panic grips area
item.description:
Clashes between the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti (JSS-Santu Larma faction) and the United People's Democratic Front (UPDF-Prasit faction) over territorial dominance in Sajek, Baghaichhari upazila of Rangamati, continued for a second consecutive day on Sunday, triggering panic among local residents.
The groups exchanged gunfire intermittently for more than two hours.
The gunfight broke out around 3:15pm in Langal Mara, near Machalong, and at Moner Chura in the South Bhaibonchhara reserve forest area of Ward No 5 of Sajek Union. No casualties were reported initially.
A similar exchange of gunfire took place in the Kalabunia area of Sajek on Saturday.
Police, local residents and public representatives said the clashes erupted over territorial dominance, with the two groups exchanging fire in the areas from around 3:15pm until 5:30pm.
Porichoy Chakma, a member of Ward No 5 of Sajek Union, told Dhaka Tribune: “Gunfire broke out around 3:15pm at Moner Chura in the South Bhaibonchhara reserve forest area. As the area is remote and has no nearby settlements, no immediate reports of casualties were available.”
Heavy gunfire erupted between the JSS and UPDF in the Kalabunia area of Ward No 5 of Sajek Union from 1pm to 4pm on Saturday. According to a reliable source, two people, one from each group, were killed in the clash. However, no organisation has confirmed the reported deaths.
Sajek Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Toffazzal Hossain confirmed that clashes between the two groups had continued for a second consecutive day.
He told Dhaka Tribune: “We have received reports that the JSS and UPDF have been exchanging gunfire for more than two hours over territorial dominance in the Langal Mara and Moner Chura areas. No casualties have been reported so far. We are looking into the matter.”
Meanwhile, following two consecutive days of clashes between the rival regional groups in the remote areas of Sajek, law enforcement agencies have stepped up security measures to bring the situation under control. The gunfights have sparked panic among local residents, who have expressed concern over the escalating tension.
Separately, two organisations have announced a one-day suspension of their blockade on the Sajek road in Rangamati. However, transport workers have opposed the decision and called a counter-blockade, creating fresh uncertainty over road communications in the area.
Vehicle movement on the Dighinala-Sajek-Baghaichhari road has remained suspended since Sunday morning as drivers and transport workers demand higher wages and allowances. However, inter-district bus services between Rangamati and Khagrachhari and other routes remain operational.

item.title: BUET, DU, BMU websites among 15 top educational institutions at cyber risk
item.description:
Several websites of some of Bangladesh’s leading educational institutions, including Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), the University of Dhaka (DU) and Bangladesh Medical University (BMU), remain vulnerable to potential cyberattacks due to unpatched security flaws in outdated versions of the PHP programming language.
The list of affected websites includes those of at least 15 prominent educational institutions, raising concerns over the security of institutional systems and potentially sensitive information related to students, faculty members and academic activities.
According to data from the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Division, more than 1,000 public and private websites across the country were initially identified as potentially vulnerable due to PHP security flaws.
The latest available information, however, indicates that more than 100 websites remain at risk. Most of them belong to private organizations, although government agencies and IT companies are also among those affected.
Among the educational institutions identified are Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB), Bangladesh Agricultural University, Asian University for Women, National University and Sonargaon University.
Websites associated with Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Rajshahi University, the Military Institute of Science and Technology (MIST), and Sapporo Dental College and Hospital have also been included in the list.
The exposure has raised concerns because university websites and associated digital platforms may contain sensitive personal and institutional information.
Departmental websites, learning management systems, admission portals and online service platforms may store students’ personal details, registration records, academic information and other institutional data.
If attackers exploit the vulnerabilities to gain unauthorized access, the confidentiality and integrity of such information could be compromised.
However, there is currently no confirmed information indicating that student data have been stolen or leaked from the identified websites.
Cybersecurity experts warn that running outdated or unsupported PHP versions can expose websites and servers to attacks, particularly when the systems are directly accessible through the internet.
Depending on the nature of the vulnerability and the server configuration, attackers may attempt to execute malicious code, gain unauthorized access to servers or take control of affected websites.
Internationally, the PHP security vulnerabilities have already triggered significant concern among cybersecurity professionals.
According to information shared by Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince, attempts to exploit the vulnerability reached several million within the first 10 hours after the issue became public.
Against this backdrop, Bangladesh's government cybersecurity agency, Bangladesh Government's e-Government Computer Incident Response Team (BGD e-GOV CIRT), issued security advisories urging public and private organizations to identify their use of PHP and take necessary protective measures.
The advisory covered government and private institutions, banks, telecommunications operators, critical information infrastructure, educational institutions and other organizations.
BGD e-GOV CIRT recommended prioritizing security updates for servers directly connected to the internet.
Where immediate updates are not possible, organizations have been advised to temporarily disable vulnerable services or restrict access while examining server logs for suspicious activities.
Institutions have also been urged to identify the PHP versions running on their websites and servers and take appropriate measures to address the vulnerabilities.
When contacted, ICT Division Secretary Md Mamunur Rashid Bhuiyan said the government was regularly alerting public and private organizations to emerging cybersecurity threats.
“Many organizations have already taken necessary measures and secured their systems after receiving the warnings. The ICT Division will also provide the necessary technical assistance to institutions that require support,” he said.
He added that instead of issuing separate warnings to individual public and private universities, the ICT Division would communicate the advisory through the University Grants Commission (UGC).
The initiative is intended to reduce the risk of information exposure involving students and other stakeholders while ensuring the security of university websites and servers.
With more than 100 websites reportedly remaining vulnerable, timely security updates, regular monitoring and stronger institutional cybersecurity measures are essential to prevent potential attacks and protect sensitive information.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir: Extended LDC graduation timeline a major diplomatic success
item.description:
Acting Foreign Minister Humaiun Kobir on Sunday said the decision to extend Bangladesh’s preparatory period for graduation from the least developed country (LDC) category by three years is a significant diplomatic success for the country.
“Extending the timeframe for LDC graduation is an important diplomatic success for Bangladesh. We achieved this success within just eight months of the formation of the government under the capable leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman,” he told UNB over the phone on Sunday.
He said they have been able to properly explain its necessity to the United Nations and the international community.
Kobir made the remarks ahead of his participation in the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), scheduled to be held in Antigua and Barbuda from November 1 to 4 as the acting foreign minister.
The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) has recently unanimously adopted a resolution granting Bangladesh a three-year extension of its preparatory period for graduation from the Least Developed Countries (LDC) category, extending the deadline to November 24, 2029.
The decision marks a significant diplomatic achievement for the current government, giving Bangladesh additional time to strengthen economic resilience, enhance export competitiveness and prepare for the eventual loss of LDC-specific trade preferences and international support measures, Bangladesh said on Friday.
Bangladesh’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations Ambassador Irene Zubaida Khan said, “Bangladesh is graduating from the LDC category not because the international process calls for it, but because graduation is an aspiration of our people. It is a national imperative, and our government is firmly committed to achieving that goal.”
Following the formation of the new government, Bangladesh formally requested the extension on 18 February 2026, citing global economic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, changing trade dynamics, energy and supply-chain risks, and domestic economic challenges.
The UN Committee for Development Policy (CDP) recommended favorable consideration of the request.
Subsequently, on July 21, the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) recommended that the General Assembly take a final decision.
To facilitate the negotiations, the government developed a three-year roadmap outlining measurable actions to ensure a smooth and sustainable transition.
The extension period will provide additional time to address structural vulnerabilities, diversify exports, improve infrastructure and logistics, and implement essential economic reforms.
The extension offers Bangladesh a crucial window to implement necessary reforms and build a more competitive, diversified and resilient economy ahead of its revised graduation date.

item.title: Dengue: Eight more die, 1,929 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Eight dengue patients died in the last 24 hours till 8:00 am today while 1,929 were hospitalized after being infected with the mosquito-borne disease during the same period.
The latest fatalities have raised the country's dengue death toll to 427 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the newly-hospitalized dengue patients, 831 were in Dhaka Division, 92 in Mymensingh Division, 257 in Chittagong Division, 259 in Khulna Division, 185 in Rajshahi Division, 73 in Rangpur Division, 213 in Barisal Division and 19 in Sylhet Division.
According to the report, a total of 136,929 dengue patients have, so far, been hospitalized across the country this year.
So far, 130,388 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in the hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the mosquito-borne disease last year.

item.title: Bangladesh Bank rolls out P2P Bangla QR payments
item.description:
In a significant leap toward achieving a fully cashless economy, Bangladesh Bank officially introduced Person-to-Person (P2P) fund transfers via the unified national standard "Bangla QR" starting Sunday, November 1.
Under the new directive, account holders across participating commercial banks, Mobile Financial Services (MFS), and Payment Service Providers (PSPs) can transfer money directly to another individual by scanning a Bangla QR code or uploading an image of a beneficiary’s QR code using their mobile banking apps.
The interoperable platform automatically identifies the destination account or wallet, eliminating the need for customers to remember or check recipient account details across different platforms.
Central bank officials highlighted that the interoperable P2P system enhances transaction security, accuracy, and convenience for everyday financial transfers nationwide.
The national implementation of P2P Bangla QR follows a series of regulatory rollouts and rapid transaction growth over recent months.
The timeline began with official administrative instructions directing all banks, MFS operators, and PSPs to integrate P2P Bangla QR functionality into their mobile applications by October 31, 2026, setting the stage for today's live launch.
This expansion builds upon dramatic transaction growth earlier in the year.
According to central bank statistics reported across media, Bangla QR adoption surged extensively through 2026, with average daily transactions climbing from roughly 100,000 (valued at over Tk28 crore) in June to approximately 350,000 transactions (valued at around Tk143.54 crore) by late September.
Ahead of the P2P launch, Bangladesh Bank introduced instant merchant payment settlements starting October 1, 2026, alongside reduced transaction costs and fee incentives for transfers up to Tk2,000.
Financial analysts noted that these coordinated regulatory shifts and the introduction of P2P QR payments are expected to foster white-label Cash-In/Cash-Out (CICO) agent models and streamline small-scale personal money transfers across the country.

item.title: Vegetable prices drop, keeps food inflation at bay
item.description:
While the prices of certain commodities are declining in the domestic market, the costs of several daily essentials continue to rise.
A drop in the prices of vegetables, alongside rice and wheat, has led to a slight improvement in food inflation.
However, prices for nutritious items such as eggs, potatoes, fish, meat, and milk remain elevated.
Coupled with high prices for fuel and import-dependent goods, this is driving up the cost of living for ordinary citizens.
According to a Bangladesh Bank report titled "Inflation Dynamics in Bangladesh: July–September 2026," average food inflation dropped to 7.13% in the first quarter of FY27, down from 8.68% in the previous quarter.
Over the same period, overall inflation decreased from 9.21% to 8.31%.
Despite the decline in food inflation, not all commodity prices have fallen.
Protein-rich foods, in particular, are seeing price increases, with these items accounting for over 51% of food inflation.
Even as food prices have eased somewhat, inflation in the fuel sector has risen.
Bangladesh Bank data shows that fuel sector inflation reached 17.4% in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, compared to 17% in the previous quarter.
Inflation for traditional fuels—such as firewood, agricultural waste, cow dung, and jute sticks—increased from 21.8% to 22.1%. Similarly, inflation for liquid fuels and lubricants rose from 13.8% to 14.7%.
The report notes that although fuel prices were hiked toward the end of September, their full impact was not yet entirely reflected in the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
Consequently, fuel sector inflation is expected to rise further in the future. Increased fuel prices could also exert upward pressure on transportation and production costs.
The contribution of import-dependent goods to domestic inflation is also on the rise.
According to Bangladesh Bank calculations, 27% of overall inflation in the first quarter of the current fiscal year stemmed from import-dependent food and non-food items, up from 24.9% in the previous quarter.
Conversely, the contribution of domestic products declined from 75.1% to 73%.
A report by the Bangladesh Trade and Tariff Commission (BTTC) highlights that tariffs and duties on import-dependent fruits—such as malta, apples, pears, and grapes—have been increased at various times, driving up their market prices.
Furthermore, rising prices of various commodities in global markets are spilling over into the domestic market.
Alongside everyday essentials, ordinary people are struggling to cope with the costs of house rent, transportation, and healthcare.
A recent survey by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) revealed that 47% of households in the country are forced to take on debt to manage household expenses.
Bangladesh Bank's report states that because the inflation rate has outpaced wage growth over the past two years, people's real incomes and purchasing power have eroded.
Although the gap between wage growth and inflation narrowed slightly in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, it began to widen again toward September, primarily driven by a slowdown in wage growth.
Overall, while the food inflation statistics show some positive movement, the overall market situation is far from comfortable.
The high prices of fuel, import-dependent goods, and protein-rich foods, combined with sluggish wage growth, continue to exert heavy pressure on the cost of living and purchasing power of ordinary citizens.

item.title: AB Bank relocates Austagram branch
item.description:
AB Bank PLC has recently shifted its Austagram branch to the second floor of the same building at its existing address.
The branch is located at Mustari Bhaban, Jamtoli, Austagram Sadar, Upazila, Kishoreganj.
Adil Chowdhury, managing director of AB Bank, inaugurated the branch at its new premises through a digital platform with a view to ensuring improved, modern, convenient and technology-driven banking services for customers.
Reazul Islam, additional managing director, and deputy managing directors of the bank were also present during the inauguration.
Officials of the bank and local dignitaries attended the inauguration ceremony at the branch premises.

item.title: Lux presents ‘Cafe Umbrella’ premieres exclusively on iScreen
item.description:
Love stories are filled with sweet moments, emotional ups and downs, misunderstandings and a wide spectrum of emotions.
Exploring these diverse dynamics of relationships is ‘Lux Presents Cafe Umbrella’, a new web film written and directed by acclaimed filmmaker Shihab Shaheen.
The web film was available exclusively on iScreen, Channel i’s OTT platform, from October 29.
Produced by Impress Telefilm and presented by Lux, ‘Cafe Umbrella’ features four distinct love stories involving four couples.
Alongside the sweetness of romance, the film explores relationship struggles, emotional conflicts, misunderstandings and the many facets of human emotions through different narratives.
These individual stories eventually come together in a common storyline.
One of the key attractions of the web film is the acting debut of the top three contestants of Lux Superstar 2025—Bidushi Barnita, Nazah Nawar and Amina Islam.
Tausif Mahbub stars opposite Bidushi Barnita, Partha Sheikh pairs up with Nazah Nawar, and Arefin Zilani appears opposite Amina Islam.
Another couple is portrayed by Saidur Rahman Pavel and Sanjida Tasnim. The film also features prominent actors Saberi Alam and Shirin Alam in important roles, along with others.
To prepare the newcomers for their roles, director Shihab Shaheen arranged a special acting workshop before filming began.
Bringing together fresh faces and experienced actors, the production aims to present familiar emotions associated with love and relationships to audiences from a fresh perspective.
Speaking about ‘Cafe Umbrella’, director Shihab Shaheen said that the web film features multiple parallel narratives, highlighting different aspects of human emotions, love and relationships.
He expects the diversity of the stories and the chemistry among the cast members to offer viewers a distinctive viewing experience.
With the debut of three new actors, four couples’ stories and Shihab Shaheen’s distinctive storytelling, ‘Lux Presents Cafe Umbrella’ has generated interest among audiences.
‘Lux Presents Cafe Umbrella’ is now available exclusively on iScreen.

item.title: Precise PetLab marks first anniversary, launches mobile app
item.description:
Precise PetLab Diagnostics & Hospital Ltd., a specialized veterinary hospital in Gulshan, Dhaka, is celebrated its first anniversary Sunday with an event at its premises, where it is also launched a mobile app.
The app will make it easier for pet owners to access the hospital’s services and their pet’s medical records.
The program began with a welcome and introduction of guests, followed by a presentation on the hospital’s facilities and innovations, a guided facility visit, and a feedback session in which guests are invited to share their views and suggestions.
Precise PetLab opened to the public on 25 August 2025 with a clear purpose: to give pet owners timely and accurate diagnosis, dependable emergency support, and treatment guided by established medical standards.
Veterinary healthcare in Bangladesh is still not fully equipped to meet these needs, so the hospital has focused on standardized emergency protocols, advanced diagnostics, and practice aligned with international guidelines.
The anniversary was an occasion to recognize the team behind this progress, introduce the hospital’s facilities to guests, and gather feedback to guide its next phase of growth.
Through the app, owners will be able to book appointments from home, reach the hospital quickly in an emergency, and view their pet’s medical records on their phone.
This will make care easier to access and more continuous from one visit to the next.
For the hospital, it will be a direct way to follow up on patients and hear from clients.
Sadia Zareen Shampa, managing director of Precise PetLab, said: “Through the implementation of our organization’s programs and initiatives, we are committed to ensuring the welfare, health, and protection of all animals across the country, whether stray, domestic, or wild.”
Precise PetLab is Bangladesh’s first 24/7 emergency veterinary hospital with a dedicated emergency unit.
It has remained open for 504 consecutive days up to 30 October, without closing even for a moment.
It is also the only veterinary hospital in the country with a dedicated emergency unit, advanced ICU, automatic ventilation and critical care.
With 15,000 square feet of space and 30 doctors, it is the largest veterinary hospital in Bangladesh.
In its first year, the hospital has served more than 4,000 appointments, attended to 1,364 emergency clients, and performed over 800 surgeries, earning the trust of pet lovers across Dhaka.
As it enters its second year, Precise PetLab remains committed to strengthening its clinical capabilities, developing its people, and raising the standard of pet healthcare in Bangladesh.

item.title: President calls for skills-based training, support for young entrepreneurs
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Sunday called for expanding skills-based training, providing financial support to small entrepreneurs and creating employment opportunities for young people to harness the country's demographic dividend.
He made the call while speaking as the chief guest at the inaugural ceremony of National Youth Day 2026 at Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka.
The President said youth are the country's most valuable human resource and the key driving force behind national development. "Bangladesh cannot move forward through political change alone," he said.
He said the country must make the best use of its large young population to strengthen its capacity and prepare for graduation from the least developed country (LDC) category, stressing the need to make young people employment-oriented and equip them with productive skills so they can contribute to the national economy.
Referring to the achievements of young entrepreneurs, including women entrepreneurs, he said many are successfully expanding their businesses and exporting products despite having limited capital. The President said the government should provide aspiring entrepreneurs with proper training and minimum financial assistance to help them become self-reliant.
He also called for expanding the programs of Department of Youth Development across the country, particularly its training and loan facilities, so that more young people can benefit.
Mirza Fakhrul emphasised the need to shift towards a need-based education system, saying greater importance should be given to vocational and technical education to meet domestic and international labour market demands.
Bangladesh can earn significantly more foreign currency if it sends skilled workers abroad, he said, adding that technical training institutions should be expanded. Highlighting the potential of biogas, the President said the technology can help rural families, particularly those involved in livestock farming, produce energy from animal waste and reduce pressure on the country's energy supply.
He also expressed concern over the growing drug addiction among young people, calling for effective measures to address the problem.
Unemployment and frustration, Mirza Fakhrul said, are among the factors contributing to drug addiction, making it necessary to create employment opportunities and raise awareness.
He urged young people to stand against violence against women, dowry and all forms of discrimination, calling for community-based organisations and movements to resist such social problems.
The President also stressed ensuring equal opportunities for young women in education, employment, entrepreneurship and leadership.
Referring to the country's political transition, he said the opportunities created through the establishment of a democratic system should be utilised for national development.
The President urged the youth never to give up and remain committed to building a self-reliant, skilled, technology-oriented and humane Bangladesh. "Never give up. We will continue our struggle and move forward," he said.

item.title: 6,000-tonne fertilizer warehouse opened in Dhaka
item.description:
Agriculture, Fisheries and Livestock Minister Mohammad Amin Ur Rashid on Sunday inaugurated a newly built 6,000-tonne fertilizer warehouse at the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) campus in Gabtoli, Dhaka.
The prefabricated steel warehouse was constructed under a BADC project to expand fertilizer storage capacity, said a press release.
BADC Chairman Md Azizul Islam presided over the inauguration ceremony, attended by Agriculture Secretary Md Selim Khan, ministry officials, BADC representatives, and fertilizer dealers.
Speaking at the event, the agriculture minister said BADC plays a vital role in ensuring farmers receive fertilizer and other agricultural inputs at fair prices and on time.
Stressing that storing fertilizer was not enough, he said ensuring its timely delivery to farmers must be the priority. Delays in supplying essential agricultural inputs could disrupt crop production, he added.
He directed officials to strengthen the entire supply chain, from storage and transportation to distribution, and ensure regular monitoring of fertilizer stocks. He also called for digitalization of inventory management and distribution systems.
The agriculture minister said more warehouses would be built in different parts of the country, including the northern region, in line with the prime minister's directives to increase storage capacity.
He further stressed the need for advance planning based on farmers' actual demand and warned against creating artificial shortages of agricultural inputs.
Saying agricultural development was key to national progress, he noted that the government was prioritizing farmers through timely fertilizer supplies, canal re-excavation, and tree-planting initiatives.
He urged BADC officials and employees to work with sincerity and accountability to ensure farmers receive fertilizer, seeds, and other essential inputs on time.

item.title: Sajek blockade partially lifted, counter-blockade disrupts traffic
item.description:
An indefinite blockade on the Khagrachhari-Sajek road in Rangamati was partially relaxed yesterday by two UPDF-backed organisations, while another group enforced a counter-blockade, disrupting traffic movement.
On the 11th day of the blockade, light vehicles were seen operating between Baghaihat Bazar and the Sajek tourist spot, allowing residents to buy essential commodities.
However, no vehicles were seen travelling to Sajek from Dighinala and Baghaichhari in Khagrachhari.
The Sajek Gono Odhikar Rakkha Committee and Sajek Karbari Association, backed by the United People's Democratic Front (UPDF), have enforced the blockade since October 22.
Citing humanitarian considerations, the two organizations announced a temporary relaxation of the blockade from morning until evening on Sunday.
However, the Parbatya Chittagong Rakkha Committee rejected the announcement and called a counter-blockade on the road.
Meanwhile, transport owners and workers announced a temporary suspension of vehicle operations.
Protesters blocked vehicles heading towards Sajek from Khagrachhari, Baghaichhari and Langadu from Sunday morning. They obstructed several points along the road by placing tree trunks and burning tyres, causing further suffering for commuters.
The two organizations had called the blockade demanding the removal of members of the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti (PCJSS) from the area.
They announced that the blockade would resume on Monday after the temporary relaxation ends on Sunday.

item.title: Ex-ambassador’s wife murdered, son sent to jail
item.description:
The son of a former Bangladesh ambassador to the Philippines has been sent to jail in a murder case filed over the death of his mother, Afia Akter, while their house help, Nargis Begum, has given a statement before a Dhaka court as a witness.
The accused, Tahsin Tarik Arnab, and Nargis were produced before the court on Sunday by the investigation officer, Dhanmondi Model police station Sub-Inspector Mohammad Touhidur Rahman.
The investigation officer filed an application seeking to keep Arnab in jail custody and another seeking to record Nargis’s confessional statement as a witness.
Following the applications, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid ordered that Arnab be sent to jail. Another Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahbub Alam, recorded Nargis’s statement, said Sub-Inspector Sharifuzzaman of the prosecution department.
While at the court, Arnab told journalists that he was a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) student at United International University (UIU).
He said he found his mother lying in the dining room in a bloodied condition early in the morning.
“There is a mosque downstairs in our building. I called the imam. I called 999, but they did not respond,” he said.
Arnab said he later spotted a police patrol vehicle while on his way to Dhanmondi Ibn Sina Diagnostic Centre and informed its personnel about the incident. The police then accompanied him to the house.
Claiming that he was ill, Arnab said his mother was a heart patient and also had diabetes.
Afia Akter, wife of the late Abul Kashem, a former Bangladesh ambassador to the Philippines, was found murdered at a flat on Road 9/A in Dhanmondi.
Her daughter, physician Nahrin Nashid Swarna, filed a murder case accusing her younger brother, Arnab.
In the case statement, Swarna alleged that Arnab was not involved in any work or occupation and frequently asked their mother for money. Whenever she refused, he would quarrel with her and threaten to kill her.
According to the case statement, at around 6:30am on Saturday, the house manager, Mahbub, called Swarna and informed her that he had learned from the building's security guard about a disturbance at their house.
Swarna immediately called the house help, Nargis. Nargis told her that Arnab had stabbed Afia Akter in the throat with a knife and left her lying in the dining room.
Swarna then asked Mahbub to take her mother to the hospital immediately. Afia Akter was taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where the on-duty doctor declared her dead.
Later, after speaking with Nargis, Swarna learned that her mother had dinner at around 9:30pm on Friday before going to sleep in her bedroom. Arnab was in his own bedroom at the time.
According to the case statement, Nargis heard Afia Akter scream at around 5:30am and went to the dining room. She saw Arnab standing with a knife in his hand, while Afia Akter was lying in a bloodied condition.
When Nargis tried to approach Afia Akter, Arnab threatened to kill her while showing her the knife. He then forced Nargis out of the house and locked the door.
After confirming his mother's death, Arnab left the house.
Police said Arnab was arrested from the Dhanmondi area after the case was filed.

item.title: Seifert blasts 93 as New Zealand win fifth India T20
item.description:
Tim Seifert narrowly missed a maiden international century but did enough to steer New Zealand to a seven-wicket win over India in the fifth and final T20 on Sunday.
Opener Seifert found some form with the bat, blasting 93 off 50 balls as the home side eased to 195-3 off 18 overs, after Adam Milne had earlier taken 4-19 to restrict the target to 192.
The result wasn't enough for New Zealand to salvage the series, which the tourists won 3-2 after winning the first three games.
New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner lamented his team's failure to win either of the first two matches, which were both tight contests in Christchurch, before finding form late in the series.
"I think those small moments in the first couple of games let us down," said Santner, referring primarily to fielding mistakes, including some important dropped catches.
"We probably could have won those games, or should have, and then the series would have looked a lot different.
"But from a cricketing point of view, there was a lot of really good stuff from our team."
Seifert had scored just 36 runs across the first four matches but the big-hitting right-hander found his touch at Seddon Park, swinging the game in New Zealand's favour by blasting 11 fours and five sixes.
He looked devastated when he played on to Nitish Kumar Reddy in the 16th over, having posted an 18th half-century before failing once again to reach three figures.
Glenn Phillips finished on 65 not out to complete an exceptional series with the bat, which included 107 when New Zealand won game four in Auckland on Friday.
Phillips's 341 runs across the five games was the most scored by any batsman in a bilateral T20 series.
The previous record was held by England's Phil Salt, who scored 331 runs against the West Indies in 2023.
Earlier, Milne's pace proved hard to handle as India were restricted to 191-8, boosted by rapid half-centuries to Ishan Kishan and captain Shreyas Iyer.
The pair combined for 93 off 7.1 overs for the third wicket after both openers fell cheaply to Milne, before Kishan departed for 61 and Iyer for 50.
Iyer said India should have pushed on to reach a higher score from
"Kishan and I created momentum but we lost back-to-back wickets," he said.
"It wasn't an easy wicket to play on, especially when the ball was seaming, but when you come overseas, you are challenged by different aspects of the game.
"We could have been better with our bowling and fielding - we were a bit sloppy."
The teams will next contest a five-match one-day international series, starting in Auckland on Wednesday, before playing two Tests.

item.title: Kane misses penalty as Bayern held by Dortmund
item.description:
Fabio Silva's 89th-minute goal earned Borussia Dortmund a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich after Harry Kane missed a penalty in a see-saw Bundesliga clash on Saturday.
Bayern were 1-0 up when Kane, playing his first match since winning the Ballon d'Or on Monday, rattled his second-half spot kick against the crossbar.
Dortmund's Serhou Guirassy levelled shortly after, but Kane helped Bayern retake the lead when he set up a Dayot Upamecano goal.
In the final minute, substitutes Konstantinos Karetsas and Silva combined to grab Dortmund a share of the spoils.
"Coming back twice here in Munich is no easy feat. We earned a well-deserved point here today," Dortmund coach Niko Kovac told Sky Germany, adding his side "never stopped believing in ourselves."
The result leaves the two sides level atop the Bundesliga table, with defending champions Bayern ahead on goal difference.
It is just the fourth time in the past 18 'Klassiker' matches that Bayern have not emerged victorious.
In addition to the late draw, Bayern, who are without Vincent Kompany as he recovers from a virus, will be concerned by further injuries to their undermanned forward line ahead of Tuesday's trip to Atletico Madrid.
Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all subbed out on Saturday, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz already out with injury.
Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the draw appeared "costly", with Saibari and Gnabry's injuries "somewhat serious".
Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich, who returned after missing three matches after the sudden death of his father, said: "It's been a really, really hard week, but you can forget during the game.
"Other than the result today, you have to say we're going through difficult moments right now, now with the injuries we picked up."
Kane was honoured pre-match with his Ballon d'Or shown to the Bayern faithful for the first time.
Dortmund thought they had taken the lead with 35 minutes gone as Jobe Bellingham scored from close range, but VAR overturned the goal for offside.
Bayern made Dortmund pay immediately when Konrad Laimer pounced on a poor Felix Nmecha pass and charged upfield to score.
Bayern were better after the break and a Nmecha handball brought Kane to the spot, but the England captain rifled his shot against the crossbar.
Moments later, Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck intercepted a Kane pass, thundered up the pitch and found Carney Chukwuemeka, who laid off for Guirassy to score at the near post.
Kane looked to have redeemed himself when he set up a goal for Upamecano, but Silva levelled in the dying stages.
Fuellkrug's fine form
Werder Bremen striker Niclas Fuellkrug continued his remarkable scoring run since returning on a season-long loan from West Ham, grabbing the opener in a 2-0 win over Hoffenheim.
Eren Dinkci also scored for Bremen but the 33-year-old Fuellkrug was the story again. By scoring in his seventh consecutive Bundesliga start, he equalled Rudi Voeller's club record from 1982-83.
"I don't score these goals to break records," Fuellkrug said, but added the mark was "nice". "It's an absolute joy to play with this group."
He has 12 goals in 10 matches in all competitions for Bremen this season, after scoring just three goals in 18 months at West Ham and one at AC Milan during a six-month loan.
RB Leipzig won 2-0 at promoted Schalke to pick up their first away points this season. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring with a penalty after 37 minutes and Romulo scored 12 minutes from time to sink the hosts.
Leipzig, who welcome Manchester City in the Champions League on Wednesday, had won all four of their home Bundesliga matches by an 18-0 aggregate but had lost all three of their away games this season.
The victory took Leipzig to fourth, one point behind third-placed Freiburg, who came from behind to win 2-1 at Augsburg.
Ermedin Demirovic scored twice as Stuttgart broke out of a funk to win 4-2 away at in-form Bayer Leverkusen.
Jamie Leweling and Bilal El Khannouss also scored for Stuttgart who had won just three of their previous eight matches.

item.title: Moreira inspires AC Milan to impressive derby victory
item.description:
AC Milan inflicted a first defeat of the season on rivals Inter Milan with a 3-1 win in a derby thriller on Saturday, as Roma cut the gap to first place to one point.
Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot struck inside the opening 10 minutes to get the Rossoneri off to a dream start before Alessandro Bastoni pulled one back.
An inspired Diego Moreira proved to be Milan's hero as the Belgian, having assisted the first two goals, swept home a free-kick late in the first half to restore a two-goal cushion as Ruben Amorim's side responded well to suffering their first league defeat of the season at home to Bologna in midweek.
"The environment is amazing," Amorim told DAZN. "The passion is completely different from any derby I have played."
"I'm really happy for the players. It was important. The fans gained a little bit more confidence in the project. We are going to have amazing nights like today and we are going to have nights like Bologna, that is part of the process."
Milan's victory stretched their unbeaten record in the famous fixture to eight games as Amorim's side moved into fourth place, four points off Inter and Lazio on top.
Roma's 5-2 win at Udinese moved them one point behind Inter in third.
Two days after plans were revealed for both clubs to move into a new stadium in 2031, the iconic 100-year-old Stadio Giuseppe Meazza was at its atmospheric best for AC Milan's 'home' game.
Milan looked fired up from the first whistle as they raced into an early lead, Pulisic heading home an inviting Moreira cross inside four minutes in the week the American signed a five-year contract extension with the Rossoneri.
Moreira was the architect again when Milan doubled their lead, fizzing a corner into the path of Rabiot, who swept a clever finish through a crowded box and in off the far post.
Inter hit back with a corner of their own midway through an electric first half when Bastoni nodded in from close range.
The goal sparked a period of dominance from the Nerazzurri, but they could not beat an inspired Mike Maignan, who produced a sharp save on Hakan Calhanoglu before an outstanding one-handed reaction stop denied Djed Spence what had seemed a certain goal.
With Inter in the ascendancy, Milan hit back against the run of play when Moreira curled a free-kick over the wall and into the top corner two minutes before the break.
The frenetic nature of the game calmed in the second half as a cagier affair unfolded, Inter probing to get back in the game as Carlos Augusto headed wide from a promising position.
An incorrect decision to award Inter a penalty for handball was overturned following a VAR intervention as the Nerazzurri were left frustrated in their hunt for another goal, Milan substitute Alphadjo Cisse instead coming closest late on with a curling strike that required a flying save from Josep Martinez.
- Roma reduce gap -
Roma blew away struggling Udinese with a rampant first-half display to claim a 5-2 away win and move one point off top.
Gian Piero Gasperini's unbeaten side moved up to 24 points, one behind joint-leaders Inter and Lazio, who can pull clear on top when they host Cagliari in Rome on Sunday.
Bryan Cristante, Rodrigo Mora, Donyell Malen and Evan Ndicka all struck before half-time and the woodwork twice denied the visitors in a dazzling show of attacking force.
Nicolo Zaniolo scored against his former club and Matteo Palma struck with a volley as Udinese improved after the break, but Daniele Ghilardi made it five in stoppage time to leave the hosts in 19th on five points after an eight-match winless run.
Earlier, Bologna claimed a third consecutive win to climb into eighth place as they came from behind to beat Monza 2-1.
League top scorer Gustavo Varela bagged his ninth goal of the season from the spot to put the visitors in front, but Tommaso Pobega and Federico Bernardeschi hit back before Bologna goalkeeper Lukasz Skorupski saved a late Patrick Cutrone penalty.

MacBook vs Windows laptops for CSE students in Bangladesh: Which is better in 2026?
item.description:
Choosing the right laptop is an important decision for computer science and engineering (CSE) students in Bangladesh. From programming assignments and database management to web development and machine learning, students need a device that can handle their coursework without putting unnecessary pressure on their budget.
The debate over MacBook vs Windows laptops for CSE students in Bangladesh largely comes down to software compatibility, performance, battery life and price. While MacBooks offer macOS and a premium portable experience, Windows laptops provide a wider range of configurations across different budgets. Understanding these differences can help students choose a laptop that meets their academic requirements and remains useful throughout their university years.
What Do CSE Students Need in a Laptop?
Most CSE programs cover programming, data structures, algorithms, databases, networking and software engineering. These subjects generally do not require an expensive laptop, but a capable processor, sufficient RAM and SSD storage can improve everyday performance.
As coursework progresses, students may need to run integrated development environments (IDEs), Android Studio, virtual machines, Docker containers and machine-learning frameworks. These applications can consume considerable system resources, especially when several tools run simultaneously.
For most students, a laptop with 16GB of RAM and a 512GB SSD provide a practical starting point if the budget allows. Students working on more demanding projects should also consider processor performance, graphics requirements and the ability to upgrade memory or storage.
How Does a MacBook Perform for Programming?
Apple's MacBook lineup runs macOS, a Unix-based operating system that supports many popular programming languages, development tools, and command-line utilities. Students can use MacBooks for Python, Java, C++, JavaScript, web development, database management, and many backend development tasks. Entry-level models like the MacBook Air M2 or the newer MacBook Air M5 handle these everyday coding tasks efficiently, while demanding workloads benefit from more powerful options like the MacBook Pro 14-inch M5.
MacBooks are particularly relevant to students interested in iOS development because Apple's Xcode development environment requires macOS. Battery life, portability and build quality can also make them attractive for university use.
However, MacBooks have limitations. Memory is generally not upgradeable after purchase, so students should choose their configuration carefully. Some Windows-specific applications may require alternatives or virtualisation. Students working with NVIDIA CUDA-dependent machine-learning projects should also know that Apple Silicon does not provide native CUDA support.
The budget is another important consideration. Students can compare different models, configurations and current prices of official MacBooks at Star Tech before deciding whether a MacBook fits their academic needs.
Windows Laptops Offer More Budget Options
Windows laptops are available across a broader range of price points, making them a practical choice for students with different financial circumstances. They support popular development tools, including Visual Studio and Microsoft's .NET ecosystem, while Windows Subsystem for Linux provides access to many Linux development tools.
Students with budgets below Tk 40,000 can explore entry-level models, including selected options from Walton and other brands. Buyers should prioritise an SSD, sufficient memory and a processor capable of handling their coursework.
With budgets below Tk 50,000, students may find additional configurations from manufacturers such as Acer and other laptop brands available in Bangladesh. Those spending below Tk 60,000 may be able to consider more capable models from HP, Lenovo, ASUS and Acer, depending on current prices and specifications.
These price ranges are indicative rather than guarantees of current availability. Students should compare individual models before purchasing, particularly if they plan to use Android Studio, virtual machines or demanding development applications.
Windows laptops also offer another advantage: selected models allow RAM and storage upgrades. Compatible laptops equipped with NVIDIA graphics can support CUDA-based machine-learning workloads, although not every CSE student needs a dedicated graphics card.
Warranty and After-Sales Support Matter
A laptop is a significant investment for many university students, so warranty coverage and repair options deserve as much attention as performance. Before purchasing, buyers should confirm the warranty period, coverage conditions and whether the device is officially sourced or imported through a third party. These details can vary by model and seller.
Trusted electronics retailers like Star Tech, a popular MacBook shop in Bangladesh, provide an online platform for comparing laptop specifications, listed prices, and available purchasing options. Students can review product details before visiting a store or completing an online purchase. Those considering instalment payments should also check the latest EMI conditions, including participating banks and applicable terms.
Which Laptop Should CSE Students Choose in 2026?
A MacBook can be a good choice for students who value portability, battery life and macOS development tools, particularly those interested in iOS application development. However, they should select memory and storage configurations carefully because upgrades are generally unavailable.
Windows laptops may be more suitable for students who want a wider choice of prices, need particular Windows applications or plan to work with compatible NVIDIA GPUs. Upgradeable hardware on selected models can also help students manage their budgets over time.
For introductory programming, either platform can be sufficient. For heavier workloads, students should prioritise the specifications required by their projects instead of choosing a laptop based only on its brand.
Ultimately, the best laptop for a CSE student in Bangladesh is one that meets university requirements, fits the available budget and offers dependable support throughout its useful life. Comparing individual models, checking software compatibility and reviewing warranty terms can help students make a more informed decision.

item.title: No more snoozing: How to master your natural wake-up time
item.description:
It is hard to find someone who does not rely on an alarm to wake up. Many people set multiple alarms on their phones to make sure they get up on time.
However, by developing a few healthy habits and aligning with the body's natural rhythm, it is possible to wake up at a specific time without relying on an alarm.
There is no strict rule that everyone must get exactly eight hours of sleep every night. Adults generally need seven to nine hours of sleep, although individual requirements may vary.
Some people feel refreshed after seven hours, while others may need as many as nine.
Therefore, the first step is to understand how much sleep your body needs. Weekends and holidays can be a good opportunity to figure this out. Try going to bed without setting an alarm and observe when you wake up naturally and how you feel afterwards.
Try to go to bed and wake up at the same time every day. Once your body becomes accustomed to a regular routine, it gradually adjusts to a fixed schedule.
As a result, your body naturally begins to relax at bedtime and prepares itself to wake up in the morning.
According to experts, your sleep schedule should be planned in a way that allows you to get enough rest regularly.
Light plays an important role in regulating the body's 24-hour internal clock, also known as the circadian rhythm. After waking up in the morning, open the curtains and let natural light enter your room.
This gives your body the signals it needs to wake up.
On the other hand, it is better to keep your bedroom as dark as possible when sleeping. You can use blackout curtains or an eye mask to block out light.
Start preparing your body and mind for rest at least one to two hours before going to bed. You can develop simple habits such as brushing your teeth, following your skincare routine, changing into comfortable clothes or reading a light book.
These activities help signal to your body that it is almost time to rest.
Sleeping in an excessively warm environment can make it difficult to get proper rest. Therefore, make sure your room is at a comfortable temperature before going to bed.
Use a fan or air conditioner if necessary. Wearing lightweight clothes and using a thin blanket can also make sleeping more comfortable.
Smartphones: Using your phone for long periods before bedtime can interfere with your natural sleep rhythm. In particular, endlessly scrolling through social media can keep your brain active for longer.
Therefore, it is best to avoid using your phone before going to sleep.
Caffeine and food: Avoid excessive caffeine consumption. Try to maintain regular mealtimes and finish dinner at least three hours before bedtime.
Alcohol: Although alcohol may help you fall asleep faster, it can disrupt the natural continuity of your sleep later in the night.
Suddenly changing your bedtime by several hours can disrupt your body's natural rhythm. Therefore, if you need to change your sleep schedule, make the adjustments gradually.
Experts suggest shifting your bedtime and wake-up time forward or backward by around 30 minutes each day until you reach your desired schedule.
Once you establish a new routine, try to follow it consistently.
Most importantly, sleep is closely connected to habits and the body's natural rhythm.
By maintaining a regular sleep schedule, getting enough natural light, following a consistent bedtime routine and reducing phone use at night, you can gradually become less dependent on alarms to wake up on time.

item.title: From tea stalls to trendy cafes
item.description:
Once, reaching for a cup of tea after waking up in the morning was a familiar habit among Bengalis. From welcoming guests and catching up with friends to office breaks and neighborhood tea stalls, tea enjoyed an unrivalled place in everyday life.
But that familiar picture is gradually changing.
Coffee is now finding its place alongside tea. From city cafes to neighborhood shops, and even ordinary tea stalls, different varieties of coffee are becoming increasingly available.
This shift in coffee consumption is no longer limited to urban lifestyles. For the younger generation, coffee has become a companion for socializing, working, studying and spending leisure time.
It is now common to see students and young professionals working on their laptops at cafes. Meanwhile, affordable instant coffee has made it easier to prepare the beverage at home, without having to visit a cafe.
Import statistics offer an indication of how rapidly coffee demand is growing in Bangladesh. According to data from the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), the country imported 139 tons of coffee in 2003. The figure rose to 264 tons in 2012. In 2025 alone, Bangladesh imported 1,745 tons of coffee.
This reflects a significant transformation in the coffee market over the past decade. According to a DAE review, the coffee market recorded an average growth rate of 56% over the last decade. During the same period, the tea market grew at an average rate of around 5%.
Although imports have fluctuated in some years due to changes in global coffee prices and import duties, the overall trend indicates growing consumer demand for coffee in Bangladesh.
One of the biggest changes behind coffee's growing popularity is its increased accessibility. In the past, coffee often brought to mind expensive cafes or a handful of specific brands. That perception has now changed. From small sachets of instant coffee to different varieties served at local cafes, coffee is now widely available.
In particular, small packets of 3-in-1 coffee have made the beverage more accessible. Requiring only hot water and a few minutes to prepare, it has become a convenient option for busy professionals and students alike. As a result, coffee is no longer reserved for special occasions but is gradually becoming a part of everyday routines.
The growing popularity of coffee has also changed the way people consume it. People no longer visit cafes simply to catch up with friends. Some work on office assignments, others study, and many attend online meetings. For freelancers and remote professionals, many cafes have become temporary workplaces.
Coffee is also becoming increasingly common at university events and gatherings among young people. Whether it is a sporting event, a cultural program, or a casual campus gathering, coffee has become a familiar companion. The growing influence of cafe culture on social media is also playing a role in increasing young people's interest in coffee.
Alongside the growing popularity of coffee, opportunities for domestic production are also emerging. Although coffee cultivation in Bangladesh first became more visible in the hilly regions, it is no longer limited to the Chittagong Hill Tracts.
According to recent reports citing information from the Department of Agricultural Extension, commercial coffee cultivation has begun not only in the three hill districts but also in Tangail, Rangpur, and Nilphamari.
Farmers in the hilly regions are also showing increasing interest in coffee cultivation. Growing market demand is creating new income opportunities for them. Increased domestic production could benefit local farmers while also helping reduce the country's dependence on imports to some extent.
Entrepreneurs are also showing growing interest in locally produced coffee. Several organizations are working with farmers in the hill regions, providing support for coffee cultivation and trying to introduce locally grown coffee to the market.
Despite the growing popularity of coffee, this does not mean that it is completely replacing tea. Instead, both beverages are finding their own places in Bangladesh's drinking culture. Some people start their mornings with tea, while others choose coffee for their afternoon gatherings. Many are also adding coffee to their regular preferences alongside tea.
Overall, coffee's place in Bangladesh's beverage culture is no longer limited to urban cafes. Its growing availability, the lifestyle of the younger generation, cafe culture, and the potential for domestic production are gradually taking coffee to a wider audience.
A beverage that many once considered an occasional indulgence is now becoming a familiar part of everyday life. In a country traditionally known for its tea culture, the story of coffee is no longer a new one; rather, it has become a visible reflection of changing lifestyles.
